summary.name: Isometric Motion Graphics. Category: Motion Design and Cinematography. Provenance: supplemental, a user-requested direction developed into prompt guidance.
summary.visualIdentity: Explicitly uses consistent isometric axes for flat graphics or shallow 3D objects, with common scale and light direction. Shows top and side faces, contact shadows, and modest thickness, while labels stay 2D. Objects never shrink with distance, because perspective is not used.
summary.suitableUses: Explicit good fits include 3D dioramas, isometric scenes with constrained movement, and layered or 2.5D artwork. Inferred fits are assembled systems, spaces, and explainers, such as infrastructure, logistics, or data pipelines. Choose this style alone when the subject is one clear assembled system or space.
summary.limitations: Adapt or omit this style when camera tilt breaks the isometric projection or adds incompatible perspective. Movement that exposes incomplete layers or breaks ground contact also requires adaptation. Layered parallax does not establish fully modeled 3D geometry. Duration, aspect ratio, resolution, and frame rate are unspecified in the source.
summary.palette: The palette is an authored, style-compatible suggestion, not an approved exact palette: background #F3EFE6, foreground #2C424F, accent_1 #63968D (teal), and accent_2 #C58662 (terracotta). Four discrete base colors are used, with gradients disabled. Task-supplied colors override these values. Foreground on background reaches 9.153:1, which passes normal text. The accents fail body-text targets (3.14 and 3.481) and are decorative only. Recheck composited frames.
summary.motionAndInteraction: Explicitly, shallow objects assemble and move along scene axes, and parallax stays restrained and spatially coherent. Motion should be smooth where it helps the action, while sharp cuts, impacts, constant-speed sections, and reading holds stay deliberate. Video state derives from composition time. Hover or focus behavior applies only to interactive HTML. Optional references are depth parallax, chapter handoffs, narrative steps, and exploded reveals; reveals apply only to separable components.
summary.audio: The source gives no fixed audio requirement. Suggestions depend on topic, audience, and narrative: background music, voiceover, sung vocals, sound effects, ambience, or silence. Explicit user audio choices and supplied assets take priority. Speech must stay intelligible, so any music or effects should not compete with narration or essential text.
summary.assetRequirements: Assets are unspecified in the source. Shallow geometry or models suit the orthographic camera. Layered artwork supports 2.5D parallax. Creature assets are needed only for an optional hop in the parallax reference. Load fonts and assets before rendering, and cache stateful simulations. Exact copy and subject details must come from the task.
summary.combinations: Explicit pairings are style-109 for isometric line-art connectors and style-095 for flat UI screens on isometric device tops. Connectors must follow the three iso axes, and objects reveal before their connections. UI must use only the primary tokens and must not skew text into the iso plane. Avoid perspective zooms that break the orthographic camera.
summary.productionApproach: Use a Three.js OrthographicCamera at a precise isometric orientation as the style renderer, and GSAP as the single owner of animated properties. HyperFrames is the default pipeline for assembly, timing, audio sync, validation, and export. Remotion is a fallback only when HyperFrames is unavailable or a verified limitation exists, and the reason must be recorded. Verify opening, action, transition, and closing frames, plus the full decoded video, loop seams, and audio sync. Distinguish simulated appearance from photographed production.
